lead.label: 6a
lead.why: Abstract names no best compound ('the cytotoxic activity of one of the isoxazole-fused spirooxindoles was evaluated in MDA-MB 468'); the text says 'compound 6a was arbitrarily chosen to examine the cytotoxic activity', so 6a is the compound of the paper's only follow-up (biological) experiment (lead rule 2).

reactions.conditions: Three-component domino reaction: isatin (1 mmol), 6-aminouracil (1 mmol), 3-phenylisoxazolone (1 mmol) in ethyl L-lactate (3 mL), room temperature, no catalyst, 60 min; precipitate filtered, washed with water; yield 95%.
reactions.source: Results text p. 8 (Scheme 3, Table 4 entry 1) and General procedure, Experimental

notes: Structure of 6a is not drawn in the text layer; the SMILES is derived from the printed name (positions 3'-phenyl, 5',7'-dione = uracil carbonyls, 6',8',9'-NH) and the standard Knoevenagel/Michael/cyclodehydration mechanism (isoxazolone C4 attached to the spiro carbon, isoxazolone C5 bearing O and bonded to the ring NH), formula C21H13N5O4 = isatin + aminouracil + phenylisoxazolone - 2 H2O. Please check OPSIN agreement; the fusion nomenclature is awkward. Reagent purchase: the paper only says 'synthetic grade chemicals from Sigma-Aldrich, Spectrochem and E-Merck were used'; 3-phenylisoxazolone has no preparation in the paper. Name of the isoxazolone is as printed in the scheme/table text ('3-phenylisoxazolone', also '3-phenyl isoxazolone'). The 6-aminouracil is printed '6-amino uracil'.
